#!/bin/sh
#SBATCH --partition=gpua100
#SBATCH --job-name=fine-tune-llama
#SBATCH --time=23:00:00
#
# LSF '#BSUB -B' (begin job immediately) has no direct equivalent in SLURM.
# Job scheduling is determined by the SLURM scheduler policy.
#
# LSF '#BSUB -N' (email on job completion) is translated to the following two lines.
# Please uncomment and set your email address.
#SBATCH --mail-type=END
#SBATCH --mail-user=your.email@example.com
#
### request the number of GPUs
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
### request the number of CPU cores (at least 4x the number of GPUs)
#SBATCH --ntasks=4
### we want to have this on a single node
#SBATCH --nodes=1
### we need to request CPU memory, too (note: this is per CPU core)
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=8G
#SBATCH --output=logs/%j.out
#SBATCH --error=logs/%j.err

module load cuda/11.6
module load python3/3.11.4

source .venv/bin/activate

export HF_DATASETS_CACHE="/work3/s212722/herd/cache"

export WANDB_API_KEY=[redacted]

# set the wandb project where this run will be logged
export WANDB_PROJECT="herd-llama"
# save your trained model checkpoint to wandb
export WANDB_LOG_MODEL="true"
# turn off watch to log faster
export WANDB_WATCH="false"

python herd/herd.py finetune_experts --config_file config_experts.ini

reasons: The combination of `--ntasks=4` and `--gres=gpu:1` is potentially incorrect for a standard single-GPU training job. This configuration launches 4 separate processes (tasks) but only provides one GPU for them to share, which can lead to resource contention or inefficient use of allocated CPUs if not handled explicitly by the application.

For a typical single-process application that needs multiple CPU cores, the standard practice is to request one task and multiple CPUs for that task (e.g., `--ntasks=1 --cpus-per-task=4`). This ensures a single process is launched with access to all 4 requested CPU cores and the GPU.
issues: The python command `python herd/herd.py ...` is not launched with `srun`. With the current request of `--ntasks=4`, only one of the four allocated tasks will execute the python script, leaving the other three tasks and their allocated resources idle.
The script specifies `--mail-user=your.email@example.com`, which is a placeholder. The user must replace this with their actual email address to receive notifications.

The output and error files are redirected to a `logs/` directory. The job will fail if this directory does not exist when the script runs. It is best practice to add `mkdir -p logs` to the script before the main execution command.
